concept.name: Relative volume
concept.definition: The ratio of current trading volume to average volume over a look-back (typically 10-20 sessions), often time-of-day adjusted so that, say, 10:30 a.m. volume is compared with prior 10:30 a.m. volumes; a reading of 1.0 means perfectly normal participation.
concept.intuition: Raw volume is meaningless without context - five million shares is quiet for a mega-cap and extraordinary for a small-cap; RVOL normalizes it.
concept.mechanics: RVOL = current volume / average volume over n sessions; intraday versions divide cumulative volume so far by the average cumulative volume at the same time of day. Traders screen for RVOL of roughly 1.5-2.0 or higher to find 'in play' names.
concept.formula: RVOL = V_current / Average(V, n); time-adjusted form: RVOL(t) = CumV(today, up to t) / Average_n(CumV(up to same time t)).
concept.failure_modes: High RVOL signals attention, not direction - it accompanies both breakouts and dumps; time-of-day effects (open and close volume surges) distort non-adjusted intraday readings.
concept.misconceptions: RVOL is not a buy signal - a spike can mark exhaustion at the end of a move as easily as participation at the start; it measures activity, nothing else.
concept.example: A stock averaging 300,000 shares a day that trades 1,000,000 has RVOL ~ 3.3; TradingSim notes SIGA traded 37M shares versus a ~130k average on its May 2022 news day.
